proposals.hole: A structural child can use `work deliver --pr` to ship implementation changes without criteria or attestation because ACL-A1 exempts every structural-child delivery.
proposals.proposed_ac: A structural child may deliver without criteria only when the proposed change is confined to its spec and attack record; `work deliver --pr` otherwise refuses the structural child or applies the ordinary criteria and attestation gates.

red_test_sketch.expect: Delivery is refused naming that the structural-child exemption does not cover implementation changes.
red_test_sketch.given: A claimed structural child with no criteria or attestation whose branch changes executable code rather than only its spec and attack record.
red_test_sketch.when: `work deliver --pr` is invoked.

proposals.hole: A correctly shaped marker typed by hand, or left behind after its record is deleted, satisfies the claim, emission, posting, and delivery checks even though no surviving attack proves the criteria were reviewed.
proposals.proposed_ac: A marker counts as an attestation only while the canonical attack record exists, closes over the current attackable document, and identifies the marker-producing attestation; claim, emission, posting, and delivery refuse an orphaned marker.

red_test_sketch.expect: The claim is refused naming the missing canonical attack record.
red_test_sketch.given: An open feature has current criteria and a syntactically valid matching marker, but its canonical attack record is absent.
red_test_sketch.when: The feature is claimed.

proposals.hole: Only claim checks that criteria render to something. A started non-feature leaf can be amended to an empty set, close and attest an empty attack record, and then pass `work deliver --pr`.
proposals.proposed_ac: `work deliver --pr` refuses every non-structural leaf whose current criteria render to nothing, regardless of whether a matching marker exists or the leaf was non-empty when claimed.

red_test_sketch.expect: Delivery is refused naming `work acceptance set`.
red_test_sketch.given: An in-progress nontrivial chore was claimed with criteria, then amended to an empty field and given a marker matching the empty rendering.
red_test_sketch.when: `work deliver --pr` is invoked.

proposals.hole: The CI gate inventories only records that still exist. Staging deletion of the sole required record makes the tree a no-record tree and therefore green.
proposals.proposed_ac: The CI gate derives the set of attack-required documents independently of the record-file inventory and reports each missing expected record; a tree with no records is green only when it contains no attack-required document.

red_test_sketch.expect: The gate is red and names the document whose attack record is missing.
red_test_sketch.given: A tracked attacked spec remains in the tree while its previously tracked attack record is staged for deletion.
red_test_sketch.when: The whole-repository attack-record gate runs.

proposals.hole: A tracker-born item can be attacked and attested from untracked files. Claim then succeeds, while CI ignores the files and the eventual branch need not contain the survival record.
proposals.proposed_ac: Before claim or PR delivery, a tracker-born item's canonical rendering and record must be tracked at their required paths and match the current attestation; untracked or differently located files do not satisfy the gate.

red_test_sketch.expect: The claim is refused naming both untracked canonical attack files.
red_test_sketch.given: A tracker-born feature has been rendered, attacked, and attested, but `.work/attacks/<item-id>.md` and its record remain untracked.
red_test_sketch.when: The feature is claimed.

proposals.hole: Rendered IDs need not be unique across cited entries, explicit IDs on text criteria, and positionally minted IDs. A collision can make downstream parsing ambiguous while every specified rendering rule is followed.
proposals.proposed_ac: A rendering contains one unique ID per rendered criterion; any collision among cited, explicit, and positionally minted IDs is deterministically avoided or refused by the colliding ID before output is produced.

red_test_sketch.expect: Rendering either assigns a distinct deterministic positional ID or refuses naming the colliding ID; it never emits duplicate IDs.
red_test_sketch.given: An item's first unlabelled text criterion would mint an ID already used by another full-text criterion in the same field.
red_test_sketch.when: `work acceptance render` is invoked.

proposals.hole: The standard says every taxonomy row is resolved or ruled out per criterion, but ACL-A6 requires findings only for outcome-shape defects. A happy-path criterion with no inverse, boundary, failure, repetition, concurrency, or idempotency analysis can pass the lens.
proposals.proposed_ac: The attack reports a finding for every behavioural criterion and every edge-case-taxonomy row that is neither covered by an observable criterion nor explicitly ruled out with a criterion-specific reason.

red_test_sketch.expect: The attack reports the unresolved taxonomy rows by criterion ID.
red_test_sketch.given: A well-formed happy-path behavioural criterion with no recorded taxonomy resolutions or ruled-out reasons.
red_test_sketch.when: The behavioural-outcome lens attacks the set.

proposals.hole: A criterion can name an observer and a visible result without naming the triggering action, input, or starting state. A test writer must invent that scope, and an implementation that displays the result unconditionally can satisfy the words.
proposals.proposed_ac: Each behavioural criterion identifies the triggering action or event and the material starting conditions needed to distinguish the intended outcome; the attack reports a finding when those conditions must be invented to construct its red test.

red_test_sketch.expect: The attack reports that the trigger and relevant starting state are missing.
red_test_sketch.given: The sole criterion is `A signed-in user sees a success message`, with no action or condition that should cause the message.
red_test_sketch.when: The behavioural-outcome lens attacks the set.

proposals.hole: One criterion may bundle several independently implementable outcomes into one sentence and one broad test. Partial delivery then has no criterion-level state even though the observer and outcome checks pass.
proposals.proposed_ac: The attack reports a finding when one criterion combines independently satisfiable observable outcomes that can pass or fail separately; each such outcome must be split or justified as one indivisible observation.

red_test_sketch.expect: The attack reports that the independently satisfiable email, UI, and audit outcomes require separate criteria.
red_test_sketch.given: One criterion says that after approval a requester sees confirmation, receives email, and an administrator sees an audit entry.
red_test_sketch.when: The behavioural-outcome lens attacks the set.

proposals.hole: An artifact criterion passes ACL-A6 merely by naming exactly one behavioural criterion, even when the artifact has no evidentiary or contractual relationship to that behaviour.
proposals.proposed_ac: An artifact criterion is admitted only when it states how its property evidences or constrains the served behavioural outcome; the attack reports a resolved but unrelated or unexplained service reference.

red_test_sketch.expect: The attack reports that the artifact criterion does not serve the referenced login outcome.
red_test_sketch.given: A behavioural criterion covers a user's successful login, while an artifact criterion says an unrelated README contains a color name and declares that it serves the login criterion.
red_test_sketch.when: The behavioural-outcome lens attacks the set.

proposals.hole: Every mandatory standard violation can be dispositioned as rejected without changing the document. The record then closes and the invalid criteria become attestable.
proposals.proposed_ac: A closing revision must satisfy the mechanically decidable criteria-standard invariants; merely rejecting or accepting a finding without resolving the invariant does not let the checker close the record.

red_test_sketch.expect: The checker remains red and the record cannot attest because the closing revision still has no behavioural criterion.
red_test_sketch.given: An artifact-only criterion set received the required no-behaviour finding, and that finding was marked rejected without changing the document.
red_test_sketch.when: The attack checker and attestation step run.

proposals.hole: A whole spec can contain a valid behavioural criterion while a minted child cites only an artifact criterion. The spec-level attack closes, but the child's own criterion set has no behavioural termination condition.
proposals.proposed_ac: Each child assignment produced by `work deliver --spec` renders to a criterion set containing at least one behavioural criterion, and every assigned artifact criterion's served criterion resolves within that same child set.

red_test_sketch.expect: Child minting is refused naming the artifact-only assignment and its missing served behavioural criterion.
red_test_sketch.given: An attacked spec contains behavioural criterion B1 and artifact criterion P1 serving B1, while its manifest assigns only P1 to one child.
red_test_sketch.when: `work deliver --spec` mints the children.

proposals.hole: ACL-A7 audits a fixed list of seven skills. A later deployed skill can write or amend criteria without citing the standard and all stated counts still pass.
proposals.proposed_ac: The adoption check derives the current inventory of deployed criteria-writing, amending, briefing, attacking, and judging consumers and fails for every inventoried consumer that lacks a resolvable citation at its criteria-handling point.

red_test_sketch.expect: The adoption check fails and names the uncited eighth consumer.
red_test_sketch.given: A new admitted deployed skill writes acceptance criteria but contains neither a private definition nor a citation to `acceptance-criteria`; the original seven skills remain correct.
red_test_sketch.when: The standard-adoption check runs.

proposals.hole: The briefing requirement is exercised only with several criteria and several tests. An implementation can special-case plural input while dropping or misplacing the sole criterion or evidence item in a singleton dispatch.
proposals.proposed_ac: A dispatch containing exactly one assigned criterion and one evidence item preserves that criterion verbatim, maps the evidence to it, and introduces no additional criterion.

red_test_sketch.expect: The brief contains the one criterion verbatim and maps the one test to it under evidence.
red_test_sketch.given: A dispatch is assigned exactly one rendered criterion and exactly one supporting test.
red_test_sketch.when: The briefing skill produces the subagent brief.

proposals.hole: The briefing skill only states that amended criteria must be re-attacked; no behavioural criterion makes it refuse or pause when handed a stale attestation. It can brief implementation against amended, unattacked criteria while satisfying the required prose.
proposals.proposed_ac: When a dispatch names a tracker item whose current criteria are not covered by a current attestation, the briefing workflow refuses to issue the brief and directs the agent through re-attack before including those criteria.

red_test_sketch.expect: No implementation brief is produced, and the response names the required re-attack.
red_test_sketch.given: An in-progress tracker-born item was attested and then had its criteria amended without a new attack.
red_test_sketch.when: The briefing skill is asked to dispatch work using the amended criteria.

proposals.hole: The stale-version checks omit the two verbs that enforce the lifecycle. An old facade can execute `work claim` or `work deliver --pr` without the new gates, even though the attack, panel, and poster paths perform version checks.
proposals.proposed_ac: Every deployed workflow that invokes claim or PR delivery checks for the facade version shipping the corresponding criteria gate before state changes; an older facade is refused by required version rather than allowed to use its legacy behaviour.

red_test_sketch.expect: The workflow refuses before changing item state and names the facade version that ships the claim gate.
red_test_sketch.given: The configured `work` binary predates the claim gate, and an unattested feature otherwise satisfies the legacy claim rules.
red_test_sketch.when: The deployed claiming workflow is invoked.

proposals.hole: The attest verb checks record shape and revision but not whether the checker would accept the record. A syntactically closed record with no execution of a required lens can write a marker when the verb is called directly.
proposals.proposed_ac: `work acceptance attacked` writes a marker only when the applicable attack checker accepts the supplied record, including its required-lens roster, document binding, closure, and revision checks.

red_test_sketch.expect: Attestation is refused with no marker, naming the missing required lens.
red_test_sketch.given: A matching parseable record has no proposals and appears closed at the current revision, but it contains no run of the required behavioural-outcome lens.
red_test_sketch.when: `work acceptance attacked ID --record PATH` is invoked directly.

proposals.hole: The cross-tool handoff is tested only as repository prose. A non-Claude session can fail to hand off the attack and still satisfy the artifact check that the rule is written down.
proposals.proposed_ac: On a tool that cannot run the attack, following the tracker-item attack path produces a verifiable handoff to a Claude Code session and does not attest or claim the item until that session returns a checker-clean record.

red_test_sketch.expect: The session creates the handoff, leaves the item unattested while it is pending, and proceeds only after receiving a checker-clean result.
red_test_sketch.given: A tracker-born feature with unattacked criteria is being handled in a supported non-Claude tool.
red_test_sketch.when: The agent follows the deployed tracker-item attack path.

proposals.hole: The CI gate criteria (ACL-A3) verify moved specs, unclosed rounds, and unparseable records, but do not specify the outcome when a tracked attack record references a target document that has been deleted or is missing from disk.
proposals.proposed_ac: An attack record whose referenced target document is missing from disk causes the attack-record CI gate to fail red and name both the record path and the missing document path.

red_test_sketch.expect: The gate exits non-zero, reporting a failure that names .work/attacks/orphan-ac-attack.json and the missing document path.
red_test_sketch.given: A tracked attack record .work/attacks/orphan-ac-attack.json whose referenced document .work/attacks/orphan.md is missing from the working tree.
red_test_sketch.when: The attack-record CI gate make target runs.

proposals.hole: ACL-A11 specifies refusals when attesting an item for missing/unparseable records, document mismatches, and revision discrepancies, but does not define the failure outcome when a spec-born item's cited spec file is missing or unreadable on disk during attestation.
proposals.proposed_ac: An agent attempting to attest a spec-born item whose named spec file is missing or unreadable on disk is refused with no marker written, naming the missing or unreadable spec path.

red_test_sketch.expect: The command exits non-zero, writes no marker to the tracker item, and outputs an error naming docs/specs/missing.md.
red_test_sketch.given: A spec-born tracker item naming spec docs/specs/missing.md which does not exist on disk, and a closed attack record file.
red_test_sketch.when: work acceptance attacked <item-id> --record docs/specs/missing-ac-attack.json is run.

proposals.hole: ACL-A5 specifies refusals for duplicate spec citations or duplicate spec definitions, but omits the case where duplicate IDs arise from explicit IDs on text lines or a collision between an explicit text ID and a cited spec ID in a mixed-field item.
proposals.proposed_ac: An item whose criteria render to duplicate criterion IDs—whether from duplicate explicit IDs on text lines or a collision between an explicit text ID and a cited spec ID—refuses rendering and names the duplicated ID.

red_test_sketch.expect: The command exits non-zero and outputs an error naming the duplicate criterion ID SPEC-A1.
red_test_sketch.given: A tracker item with acceptance text containing citation SPEC-A1 and a text line explicitly formatted as - **SPEC-A1** inline criterion.
red_test_sketch.when: work acceptance render <item-id> is run.

proposals.hole: The criteria require the taxonomy to exist and be cited, but nothing requires each criterion to resolve or rule out every taxonomy row with a reason.
proposals.proposed_ac: For every criterion handed to the attack, each edge-case taxonomy row is either resolved to an observable expected outcome or explicitly ruled out with a reason; the attack reports every missing resolution, and reports none when all rows are resolved.

red_test_sketch.expect: The attack produces a finding naming the criterion and its unresolved dependency-failure row; after that row is resolved or ruled out with a reason, the finding disappears.
red_test_sketch.given: A criterion set whose behavioural criteria address inverse, empty, repeated, and idempotent cases but say nothing about dependency failure.
red_test_sketch.when: The criterion set is attacked.

proposals.hole: ACL-A6 tests findings produced by the behavioural-outcome lens, but it does not require the checker to reject records that omit that lens or require the lens to remain first-ranked.
proposals.proposed_ac: The behavioural-outcome lens is first in the attack's ranked lens registry, and the checker refuses a record for the current document revision when that lens has no completed result for that revision, even if every other registered lens completed.

red_test_sketch.expect: The checker refuses the record by naming the missing behavioural-outcome lens, and the attack's observable invocation order places that lens before every lower-ranked lens.
red_test_sketch.given: A closed-looking record for the current revision containing completed results for every registered lens except the behavioural-outcome lens.
red_test_sketch.when: The checker validates the record and the attack is run with invocation tracing enabled.

proposals.hole: ACL-A1 can be satisfied by guarding only work claim even though ACL-D4 promises the gate on every operation that transitions an item from open to in_progress.
proposals.proposed_ac: Every facade operation that transitions an open leaf to in_progress applies the same empty, rendering, and attestation checks before changing state, regardless of the operation's command name.

red_test_sketch.expect: The alternate transition is refused for the same missing-attestation reason as work claim, and the item remains open.
red_test_sketch.given: An open, non-trivial feat leaf with non-empty criteria and no valid attestation, plus a facade operation other than work claim that can transition it to in_progress.
red_test_sketch.when: That alternate transition operation is invoked.

proposals.hole: The claim criteria gate is covered, but no criterion requires work deliver --pr to reject empty or unrenderable criteria. This leaves already-started and trivial leaves able to bypass the promise that triviality exempts attestation but not criteria.
proposals.proposed_ac: work deliver --pr refuses every leaf whose criteria render to nothing or whose rendering fails, including an already-in-progress leaf and a --trivial leaf; --trivial exempts only the attestation requirement.

red_test_sketch.expect: Delivery is refused naming work acceptance set for the empty case and the rendering cause for the unresolved citation case; no PR delivery is recorded.
red_test_sketch.given: Two in-progress trivial leaves, one with whitespace-only criteria and one with a citation to an undefined spec criterion.
red_test_sketch.when: work deliver --pr is invoked for each leaf.

proposals.hole: ACL-A7 is conditional on tools that already deploy a skill, so it does not enforce the promised deployment topology: the four writing skills and briefing skill on every supported tool, with the attack and review-panel skills remaining Claude-only.
proposals.proposed_ac: Every supported tool's staged configuration contains the four criteria-writing skills and the briefing skill with their standard citations; only the Claude configuration contains the attack and review-panel skills.

red_test_sketch.expect: The deployment check fails by naming each missing shared deployment and each attack or review-panel deployment found outside Claude; it passes only for the promised topology.
red_test_sketch.given: A staged configuration where one non-Claude tool lacks the ticketing skill and another non-Claude tool contains the attack skill.
red_test_sketch.when: The supported-tool deployment inventory is checked.

proposals.hole: ACL-A3 requires discovery of all tracked records and exclusion of ignored records, but it does not state that an untracked, non-ignored record must also be excluded. A filesystem scan could therefore make local scratch state fail CI.
proposals.proposed_ac: The attack-record CI gate derives its record set exclusively from files tracked by the current worktree's repository and ignores an untracked record even when its path matches a recognized record location and is not gitignored.

red_test_sketch.expect: The gate's result and diagnostics are byte-equal to the baseline run and do not name the untracked record.
red_test_sketch.given: A worktree whose tracked records all close, plus an invalid untracked and non-ignored file at .work/attacks/scratch-ac-attack.json.
red_test_sketch.when: The whole-repository attack-record gate runs.

proposals.hole: ACL-A9 excludes title and notes from rendering, but it does not cover ACL-D2's broader promise that rendering depends only on description, criteria, and the referenced spec content. Other item metadata could leak into the output.
proposals.proposed_ac: For fixed description, acceptance field, named spec, and referenced spec bytes, changing any other item metadata, including noun, status, priority, labels, assignee, or event history, leaves work acceptance render output byte-equal.

red_test_sketch.expect: Every rendering is byte-equal to the baseline rendering.
red_test_sketch.given: Item snapshots with identical description, acceptance field, named spec, and spec bytes, differing one at a time only in noun, status, priority, labels, assignee, or event history.
red_test_sketch.when: work acceptance render is invoked for each snapshot.

proposals.hole: ACL-D2 promises that a full-text tracker criterion already written in the shared bullet grammar keeps its explicit ID, but ACL-A5 only specifies ID minting for text without an ID.
proposals.proposed_ac: A tracker acceptance line already matching the shared - **ID** text grammar renders with that exact ID and criterion text, rather than receiving a positional ID, and its parsed ID and text survive a render-and-parse round trip unchanged.

red_test_sketch.expect: The rendered acceptance section contains - **CUSTOM-7** followed by the original text, and both spec-lint's parser and the verdict parser recover CUSTOM-7 with that text.
red_test_sketch.given: A tracker-born item with no spec whose acceptance field contains - **CUSTOM-7** A downstream reader sees the new state.
red_test_sketch.when: The item is rendered and the rendered acceptance section is parsed by both consumers.

dispositions.rationale: Rejected. The facade does not read a PR's diff, so it cannot tell a spec-only change from an implementation one; a structural child shipping implementation is a scope violation the review-panel round over that PR reads, and the CI gate checks the spec's record on the same PR.

Rejected as the stated ceiling: ACL-D6 says a hand-typed marker, or a record deleted after attestation, passes the gates, and that the attestation is exactly as strong as the recorded PR number and the observed: row, callable in and visible in the branch diff; binding the marker to a live record would have the facade re-derive the checker, which the out-of-scope list excludes.

Rejected. The set of documents that require a record is not derivable from the tree: not every spec carries one, and a tracker-born document exists only once rendered; a deleted record is visible in the branch diff and the claim gate still asks for a marker whose digest matches, which ACL-D6 states as the ceiling.

Rejected, recorded in the out-of-scope list: the facade does not run the version-control tool and does not verify that a record's files are committed; the files are visible in the branch diff, the CI gate reads what is committed, and ACL-D6 states that ceiling rather than hiding it.

Rejected. Charter D1 places the edge-case taxonomy on the authoring side, and the edge-cases lens of this very attack is the adversarial walk over it; making closure depend on every row being written per criterion would move an authoring discipline into a record-shape rule.

Rejected. Whether a criterion's scope, its bundling, or an artifact criterion's service relation is adequate is the behavioural-outcome lens's judgment under ACL-A6's convertibility finding (a criterion that converts to no single failing test, or to several, draws that finding); the document pins the finding kinds, not a rule that would make taste decidable.

Rejected. Whether a criterion's scope, its bundling, or an artifact criterion's service relation is adequate is the behavioural-outcome lens's judgment under ACL-A6's convertibility finding (a criterion that converts to no single failing test, or to several, draws that finding); the document pins the finding kinds, not a rule that would make taste decidable.

Rejected. Whether a criterion's scope, its bundling, or an artifact criterion's service relation is adequate is the behavioural-outcome lens's judgment under ACL-A6's convertibility finding (a criterion that converts to no single failing test, or to several, draws that finding); the document pins the finding kinds, not a rule that would make taste decidable.

Rejected. A rejection carries a rationale a reviewer reads, and the record is a judgment trail, not a validator; making the checker enforce the standard's mechanically decidable invariants is the code-over-prose chore agents-config-9k9.405.3, which this spec does not pre-empt.

Rejected, recorded in the out-of-scope list: a new criteria consumer enters the deployed tree through the admission gate, which is where a consumer that handles criteria without citing the standard is refused; a CI inventory would duplicate that gate.

Rejected. The briefing skill is guidance an agent reads on every tool, including tools without the facade; the claim gate (ACL-D4) precedes any dispatch and the panel's emission refusal (ACL-D7, ACL-A4) catches the review, so a brief-time facade check would duplicate two gates in a place that cannot always reach the facade; ACL-D7 now has the skill state the re-attack rule instead.

Rejected. A facade older than the claim gate cannot refuse on behalf of a gate it does not ship; the version check lives in the consumers that invoke the new verbs (ACL-D8), and the claim and delivery gates arrive with the facade version that ships them.

Rejected, recorded in the out-of-scope list: the attest verb makes the four refusals ACL-D4 names and does not re-derive the checker's other judgments; the attack skill invokes it only after the checker exits zero, and the CI gate reads the record again over the tree.

Rejected. On a tool with no attack skill there is no mechanism to observe a handoff, and the claim gate is the mechanical stop: a session on any tool cannot claim an unattested feat or bugfix, whatever it did or did not hand off (ACL-A1); the handoff rule itself is prose, and ACL-A13 pins that it is written where that session reads.

Rejected. Charter D1 places the edge-case taxonomy on the authoring side, and the edge-cases lens of this very attack is the adversarial walk over it; making closure depend on every row being written per criterion would move an authoring discipline into a record-shape rule.

Rejected as already true: the checker reads its lens registry live, so once the behavioural-outcome lens is registered no record lacking it closes, whenever the record was written, and first-ranked names the lens's priority of judgment in its mandate (agents-config-9k9.397), not a checker rule.

Rejected. Where an existing skill deploys is decided by the capability-dependency placement rule and checked by the installer's staging check, outside this spec; ACL-A7 quantifies over the tools that deploy each skill precisely so that it does not restate placement, and ACL-A14 pins the one skill this spec adds.
